stories.title: Barings Acquires Ralphs-Anchored Center from First Washington
stories.excerpt: CBRE arranged the $66.2-million sale of Village Center at Rose, a 118,876-square-foot, Ralphs-anchored shopping center at 600-858 N. Rose Dr. in Placentia. Barings acquired the fully leased property from First Washington Realty. Jimmy Slusher, Mark Damiani, James Tyrrell and Shaya McClanahan of CBRE’s National Retail Partners – West represented the seller. Built in 1996, Village Center at Rose sits on 10.15 acres at the northeast corner of North Rose Drive and Alta Vista Street. Ralphs, which has operated at the center since it opened, occupies 37% of the gross leasable area. Eighty percent of existing tenants have occupied the property for more than 10 years. “The center serves a dense trade area with strong household incomes and limited new retail supply,” Damiani said. “More than 147,000 people live within three miles of the center, and nearby new housing continues to add to the demand that Ralphs and the surrounding tenants serve.” The post Barings Acquires Ralphs-Anchored Center from First Washington appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Barings acquires $66.2M Ralphs-anchored center, Placentia, Orange County.
147,000 residents within 3 miles; 80% tenancy >10 years; limited new retail supply.
Property fully leased; anchored tenant since 1996 opening.
stories.summary: Barings acquired Village Center at Rose, a 118,876-sq-ft grocery-anchored shopping center in Placentia, Orange County, for $66.2 million ($557/sf) from First Washington Realty. Ralphs has anchored the property since opening in 1996 and occupies 37% of GLA; 80% of existing tenants have remained for over 10 years. The center serves 147,000 people within a 3-mile radius in a supply-constrained retail market with strong household incomes.
stories.impact: Strong demographic fundamentals and retail supply constraints in Orange County support rental demand for nearby multifamily. New housing development mentioned in the article signals population growth in the trade area, which should translate to sustained demand for apartments in Placentia and surrounding submarkets, supporting future development economics.

stories.title: Madison Realty Lends $463M for First St. Regis Condo in Sunny Isles, Fla.
stories.excerpt: Fortune International Group and Château Group have secured a $463 million construction debt package from Madison Realty Capital to complete the St. Regis Residences condo development in Sunny Isles Beach, Fla. The oceanfront project at 18801 Collins Avenue will include two 62-story skyscrapers. The debt package will refinance the existing debt from Bank OZK, which has issued $418 million for the development since 2024, and provide the financing to complete the construction of the so-called South Tower, which broke ground in 2023. The 170-unit skyscraper is expected to be completed by the end of 2028, according to a representative for the sponsors. So far, 80 percent of units have presold, generating over $1.6 billion. Construction has yet to start for the 150-unit North Tower, though it did secure $114 million in financing from City National Bank of Florida earlier this year. Berkadia’s Scott Wadler, Michael Basinski, Mitch Sinberg, Matt Robbins, Brad Williamson and Matthew Monahemi arranged the recent financing from New York-based Madison Realty Capital. “This transaction reflects our conviction in the Sunny Isles Beach submarket,” Josh Zegen, co-founder and managing principal of Madison Realty Capital, said in a statement. “Demand at the top of the market is increasingly concentrated in projects that pair oceanfront scarcity with the service and amenities of a five-star hotel.” Last year, the lender supplied $630 million for Gil Dezer to finish the Bentley-branded, oceanfront condo skyscraper nearby. The construction debt was South Florida’s largest loan issued for a luxury condo in 2026. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Madison Realty $463M construction loan for St. Regis Residences, Sunny Isles, Fla.
South Tower 170 units; 80% presold ($1.6B); completion end 2028.
Refinance of $418M Bank OZK debt; North Tower 150 units not yet started.
stories.summary: Fortune International Group and Château Group secured $463 million in construction debt from Madison Realty Capital to complete the St. Regis Residences oceanfront condo project in Sunny Isles Beach, Florida. The South Tower (170 units) broke ground in 2023 with 80% presold ($1.6 billion in sales) and expected completion by end of 2028; the North Tower (150 units) has not yet commenced construction. The financing refinances existing $418 million Bank OZK debt.
stories.impact: South Florida condo presales momentum and strong capital availability signal robust high-end residential demand in Miami-Dade, but the slow North Tower timeline suggests developer/lender caution on speculative starts. For rental developers, this signals competition for high-end units will intensify post-2028, but near-term multifamily demand remains robust with luxury for-sale absorption still ramping.

stories.title: JLL Arranges Financing for Lightstone Acquisition on Upper West Side
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged acquisition financing for Lightstone’s purchase of 323 W. 96th St., a 174-unit multifamily property on Manhattan’s Upper West Side. Senior managing director Peter Rotchford and managing director Michael Shmuely worked on behalf of Lightstone to secure the financing from MF1, a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire Residential Investments. Lightstone is acquiring the property from Pinnacle Group for a reported $88 million. Located between Riverside Park and West End Avenue, 323 W. 96th is a 15-story, 174-unit rental building. The 136,651 square-foot property was built in 2004. “323 W. 96th St. is a well-located asset with strong existing demand, an experienced sponsor and a clear business plan for creating additional value,” said Rotchford. “There continues to be significant lender appetite for high-quality multifamily opportunities, particularly in supply-constrained New York City neighborhoods. MF1 understood both the strength of the Upper West Side fundamentals and Lightstone’s plan for the property, allowing us to structure financing that supports the acquisition and Lightstone’s investment in the asset.” The post JLL Arranges Financing for Lightstone Acquisition on Upper West Side appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lightstone acquires 174-unit Upper West Side rental for $88M.
MF1 (Berkshire Residential) financing; property built 2004, 136,651 sq ft.
Strong demand and supply-constrained NYC fundamentals cited by lender.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged acquisition financing for Lightstone's $88 million purchase of 323 W. 96th Street, a 174-unit multifamily building on Manhattan's Upper West Side built in 2004. Financing sourced from MF1, a Berkshire Residential Investments subsidiary. The property sits between Riverside Park and West End Avenue with strong existing demand; lender emphasized continued appetite for high-quality multifamily in supply-constrained NYC neighborhoods.
stories.impact: Continued institutional investor appetite for stabilized Upper West Side rentals reflects sustained demand in supply-constrained Manhattan. This validates hold-and-reposition strategies in established neighborhoods; however, limited new supply pipeline and strong incumbent ownership make acquisition-based value creation difficult—new development or adaptive reuse remain the primary paths to ground-up multifamily growth in Manhattan.

stories.title: National City Investment Group Commences Workforce Housing Build
stories.excerpt: The National City Investment Group, a locally owned, privately held real estate investment company, recently broke ground on Market View, a 120-unit multifamily residential community located at 303 Highland Ave. in National City. The development will transform an underutilized parking lot adjacent to Manolo Farmers Market, which has served National City for more than 33 years, into a residential community. Market View is scheduled for completion in the first quarter of 2028. “By bringing much-needed housing to National City, the National City Investment Group is helping create a more vibrant, walkable community that supports local businesses, and contributes to the continued revitalization of the area,” said Paul Najar, EVP, Gafcon PM-CM LLC, which is providing real estate advisory and project management services for the development. Designed by RDC with R.D. Olson Construction serving as the general contractor and McCullough Landscape Architecture handling landscape design, Market View will offer workforce housing in three distinct residential buildings linked by open space, pedestrian connectivity and Manolo Farmers Market. The post National City Investment Group Commences Workforce Housing Build appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: National City Investment Group breaks ground, Market View 120-unit workforce housing.
National City, California; completion Q1 2028; parking lot conversion.
RDC design; R.D. Olson Construction GC; walkability focus near farmers market.
stories.summary: National City Investment Group commenced construction on Market View, a 120-unit workforce housing community at 303 Highland Avenue in National City, California, transforming an underutilized parking lot. Designed by RDC with R.D. Olson Construction as general contractor, the project will be completed in Q1 2028 and includes three residential buildings linked to the adjacent Manolo Farmers Market for pedestrian connectivity and community revitalization.
stories.impact: Workforce housing development in smaller California markets signals gap in supply and acceptable development economics despite higher construction costs. Success of this project may attract further multifamily capital to underserved South County markets; infill parking lot conversion model de-risks entitlements and land cost, making feasibility stronger than greenfield sites in the region.

stories.title: Report: Seattle-Tacoma Area Office Market Sees Declining Vacancy
stories.excerpt: The Seattle-Tacoma metro area office is showing signs of declining vacancy, according to a recent report by Marcus & Millichap. “Seattle-Tacoma’s office market is showing broader signs of stabilization as improving absorption and a nearly empty development pipeline support declining vacancy, although recovery continues to vary by property class and submarket,” said Joel Deis, senior managing director, market leader. Key findings of the report include that approximately 2.8 million square feet of office space was absorbed on net during the year ended in June, lowering vacancy from a peak of 19.7% in the second quarter of 2025 to 18.6%. Development will be virtually nonexistent in 2026, with only two properties totaling 35,000 square feet scheduled for completion. The previously anticipated delivery of Amazon’s roughly 1 million-square-foot Bellevue 600 Tower 1 is no longer expected this year.The 2026 forecast calls for vacancy to decline 80 basis points to 18.4% and average asking rent to increase 0.8% to $29.30 per square foot by year-end, although downtown rents may continue to face downward pressure. The post Report: Seattle-Tacoma Area Office Market Sees Declining Vacancy appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Seattle-Tacoma office vacancy declined 110 bps to 18.6% YoY; 2.8M sf absorbed.
2026 pipeline only 35,000 sf; Amazon Bellevue 600 Tower 1 (1M sf) delayed indefinitely.
Forecast: 80 bps vacancy decline 2026 to 18.4%; 0.8% rent growth.
stories.summary: The Seattle-Tacoma metro office market showed stabilization with vacancy declining from 19.7% (Q2 2025) to 18.6%, absorbing 2.8 million square feet net during the year ended June. The development pipeline is virtually empty for 2026 with only 35,000 square feet scheduled for completion; Amazon's anticipated 1 million-square-foot Bellevue 600 Tower 1 is no longer expected to deliver this year. Forecasts predict 80 basis points of additional vacancy decline in 2026 with asking rents rising 0.8%.
stories.impact: Collapse of office pipeline in Seattle-Tacoma removes supply competition and supports positive rent trajectory, which benefits corporate tenant recruitment—a leading indicator of stronger job growth and in-migration to support multifamily demand in 2026–2027. Amazon's indefinite delay signals tech hiring moderation, but office stabilization and tight supply should sustain baseline apartment demand in Bellevue and greater Seattle submarkets.

stories.title: Chemical Manufacturer Renews Office Lease in Parsippany
stories.excerpt: Signature Acquisitions, an owner and manager of suburban office space throughout New Jersey and suburban New York, has signed AdvanSix to an 18,000-square-foot lease renewal at 300 Kimball Dr., the firm’s 400,000-square-foot, Class A office property in Parsippany, NJ. Formerly a division of Honeywell, AdvanSix produces nylon solutions, plant nutrients and chemical intermediates. “New Jersey has a strong ecosystem of innovative companies and our properties are ideal corporate homes for tenants whose businesses reflect where the economy is headed,” said Sandy Monaghan, SVP of Signature Acquisitions. “For companies like AdvanSix, location, accessibility and amenities matter, and their renewal at 300 Kimball is a strong vote of confidence in both the building and our proficiency as operators.” Signature Acquisitions signed 23,500 square feet of leases between July and September 2026: the deal with AdvanSix as well as new leases with NTG Air & Ocean at 6 Commerce Dr. in Cranford, and with MTV Foods at Waterview Plaza in Parsippany. The post Chemical Manufacturer Renews Office Lease in Parsippany appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AdvanSix renews 18,000 sf at Parsippany; Signature Acquisitions Class A office.
23,500 sf leased July–Sept 2026; three separate tenant commitments NJ/NY suburbs.
AdvanSix (formerly Honeywell division) produces chemicals, nylon, plant nutrients.
stories.summary: Signature Acquisitions signed AdvanSix, formerly a Honeywell division, to an 18,000-square-foot lease renewal at 300 Kimball Drive in Parsippany, New Jersey. Between July and September 2026, Signature signed 23,500 square feet of leases across three properties, including deals with NTG Air & Ocean and MTV Foods. AdvanSix produces nylon solutions, plant nutrients, and chemical intermediates.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact. Parsippany office renewal reflects stable suburban NJ market and corporate retention, but does not signal major job growth or population in-migration. Indirectly, retention of established manufacturers in the region provides steady baseline employment stability supporting multifamily demand, but no new catalyst for rental growth.

stories.title: Shorenstein Signs 78K SF in Office Leases at Repositioned D.C. Building
stories.excerpt: Shorenstein announced Monday that it has secured approximately three office leases totaling 78,000 square feet at its recently repositioned building in Washington, D.C.’s East End. Policy analysis and consulting firm Capstone signed the largest lease at approximately 43,000 square feet. Government relations and lobbying firm Monument Advocacy signed for 25,000 square feet, and the nonprofit Skoll Foundation signed for 10,000 square feet, according to Avison Young, which represented Shorenstein. The brokerage did not disclose the lengths of the leases or the asking rents at the property. Shorenstein acquired the property at 901 K Street NW in June 2025 for $84.3 million, property records show, and spent the past year upgrading the building. Improvements include a renovated lobby, a new conference and event center, enhancements to the rooftop terrace and expanded tenant amenities. “The leasing momentum at 901 K Street is the result of the market’s continued flight to quality,” Avison Young’s Jonathan Wellborn said in a statement. Wellborn, Eli Barnes and Will Stern of Avison Young’s D.C. agency leasing team represented Shorenstein in the transactions. “Companies are investing in workplaces that help attract talent, strengthen culture and support collaboration,” Barnes said. “901 K Street delivers that experience through its prime location, upgraded amenities and vibrant retail offerings.” Shorenstein specializes in acquiring and repositioning office and mixed-use properties across major U.S. markets. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Shorenstein leases 78,000 sf at repositioned 901 K Street NW, Washington, D.C.
Capstone (policy/consulting) 43K sf; Monument Advocacy 25K sf; Skoll Foundation 10K sf.
Acquired June 2025 for $84.3M; lobby, rooftop, conference center renovated.
stories.summary: Shorenstein announced three office leases totaling 78,000 square feet at its recently repositioned building at 901 K Street NW in Washington, D.C.'s East End. Capstone (policy analysis/consulting) signed the largest lease at 43,000 square feet, followed by Monument Advocacy (government relations) at 25,000 square feet and Skoll Foundation (nonprofit) at 10,000 square feet. Shorenstein acquired the property in June 2025 for $84.3 million and invested in a renovated lobby, new conference center, and enhanced amenities.
stories.impact: D.C. East End office recovery signals 'flight to quality' supporting repositioning economics; however, policy/consulting and advocacy tenant clusters do not imply major job growth or wage-scale in-migration. Multifamily exposure limited unless East End revitalization drives broader neighborhood amenity/transit improvements that attract younger workforce renters seeking walk-to-work proximity to K Street corridor employment.

stories.title: Octagon Lends $48M on Missouri Office-to-Resi Conversion of Former 7Up HQ
stories.excerpt: A building that forged the rise of a soda brand in the 1960s and `70s is poised for a fizzy makeover with some fresh creative capital. A joint venture between Revive Capital Development and KAI Design + Build has secured $48.25 million of construction financing to facilitate an office-to-residential conversion of the former 7Up global headquarters in Clayton, Mo., Commercial Observer has learned. The financing package includes tax credits for historic rehabilitation. Octagon Finance provided the unitranche loan supporting the adaptive reuse of the 11-story building in Downtown Clayton 10 miles west of St. Louis into a 118-unit apartment complex. The 200,000 square-foot redevelopment project called the Upton will be built at the site where 7Up launched its Uncola campaign in 1968. Zach Bubrosky, head of originations for Octagon Finance, said adaptive reuse was an ideal solution for the former 7Up building given the historic nature of the property and the need for new housing options or young professionals in an area close to Washington University in St. Louis. The soda company relocated from Clayton to Dallas in the late `70s, and the building has been vacant for more than a decade. “When you’re doing these historic tax credit projects, you have to maintain the historic integrity of the building,” said Bubrosky, noting that the building will have pictures of various 7Up bottles. “It makes for an interesting project while also giving back to the community in a way by providing additional housing at a time when you know there’s such a lack of housing supply in this market.” Located at 121 South Meramec Avenue, the Upton will have a unit mix of studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom apartments. Resident amenities will include a fitness center, a heated outdoor spa, a dog wash, a game room and fire pits. bullets: Octagon $48.25M construction loan for office-to-resi conversion, Clayton, Missouri.
Former 7Up HQ (200K sf, 11-story) converts to 118-unit apartments, The Upton.
Historic tax credits included; completion timeline not disclosed; 10 miles west St. Louis.
stories.summary: A joint venture between Revive Capital Development and KAI Design + Build secured $48.25 million in construction financing from Octagon Finance to convert the historic 11-story former 7Up global headquarters in Clayton, Missouri into 118 multifamily units called The Upton. The 200,000-square-foot adaptive reuse project benefits from historic rehabilitation tax credits and is positioned to serve young professionals in the suburban St. Louis market.
stories.impact: Office-to-resi conversion signals declining suburban office demand near St. Louis and demonstrates developer pivot toward residential use of Class A office stock. Tax-credit-backed financing shows lender appetite for adaptive reuse; success of The Upton may attract further conversion capital to Clayton and broader St. Louis suburbs, increasing multifamily supply but also absorbing institutional capital that might otherwise deploy to new construction.

stories.title: AI Firm Minerva Doubles Office Footprint at the Refinery at Domino
stories.excerpt: Two Trees Management has signed a deal with an artificial intelligence firm to more than double its office space on the Williamsburg, Brooklyn, waterfront, Commercial Observer has learned. Data platform Minerva BI, which stands for business intelligence, expanded from 3,500 square feet on the third floor of the Refinery at Domino to 8,320 square feet on the 10th floor of the new-ish development, according to tenant broker Cushman & Wakefield. Two Trees did not immediately disclose the length of the lease, but asking rent in the building ranges from $68 to $86 per square foot. “Minerva’s expansion at the Refinery reflects both the company’s impressive growth trajectory and the continued appeal of the building to like-minded innovative technology firms,” C&W’s Sam Hoffman, who represented the tenant, said in a statement. “There was significant interest from other expanding tenants within the building, so securing this space required us to move quickly and strategically. We were able to position Minerva ahead of competing demand and secure the additional space needed to support its next phase of growth.” Two Trees had in-house representation in the transaction. “It has been a pleasure to see Minerva expand its footprint at the Refinery and enter its next phase of growth,” Alyssa Zahler, managing director of commercial leasing for Two Trees, said in a statement. “Companies like Minerva are an important part of the innovative technology and AI community that makes the Refinery such a dynamic place to work.” Other tenants in the revitalized Brooklyn sugar factory include event space operator Skylight, which expanded to 13,600 square feet in May, and AI-driven marketing support platform Mega, which signed a 3,926-square-foot lease in December 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Minerva BI expands 3,500 sf to 8,320 sf at Refinery at Domino, Williamsburg.
AI/data platform firm more than doubles office footprint; asking rent $68–$86 psf.
Two Trees Management landlord; robust tenant interest; Cushman & Wakefield represented.
stories.summary: Minerva BI, an AI and data platform firm, expanded its office footprint from 3,500 to 8,320 square feet at Two Trees Management's Refinery at Domino in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. Asking rent ranges from $68 to $86 per square foot; significant competing tenant interest required the deal to move quickly. The expansion reflects the firm's strong growth trajectory and continued appeal of the mixed-use property to innovative technology tenants.
stories.impact: Tech tenant expansion in Williamsburg indicates sector strength and continued rent-paying capacity in Brooklyn's prime office submarkets. Strong competition for office space may offset some multifamily development upside if tech companies absorb significant mixed-use floorplate, but rising office rents and tech payroll also drive discretionary spending and rental demand for nearby residential product—net positive for adjacent multifamily development.

stories.title: Barings Buys SoCal Grocery-Anchored Shopping Center for $66M

First Washington Realty sold the Village Center at Rose, a 118,876-square-foot retail property at 600-858 North Rose Drive in Placentia, Calif., CBRE announced Monday. The transaction is equal to about $557 per square foot. The 10.15-acre shopping center was built 30 years ago at the northeast corner of North Rose Drive and Alta Vista Street. Kevin Miller, Barings’ head of U.S. real estate acquisitions said the deal for Village Center at Rose further advances the firm’s strategy focused on “necessity-based retail” and strengthening portfolio income durability and cash flow visibility. “The property’s established tenant base, strong occupancy and location in a supply-constrained market align well with our investment approach,” Miller said in a statement. Approximately 80 percent of the existing occupants have operated at the center for more than a decade. Supermarket chain Ralphs, which has anchored the property since its opening with 44,000 square feet, or about 37 percent of its leasable space. Other tenants include Jersey Mike’s Subs, The UPS Store, Cold Stone Creamery, WaBa Grill, Chase Bank, Carl’s Jr., Carbon Health, Phenix Salon Suites and Australian Swim School. “The center serves a dense trade area with strong household incomes and limited new retail supply,” CBRE’s Mark Damiani said in a statement. “More than 147,000 people live within three miles of the center, and nearby new housing continues to add to the demand that Ralphs and the surrounding tenants serve.” The surrounding five-mile trade area contains more than 372,700 residents, with an average household income of approximately $154,800, according to CBRE. Ralphs, which anchors 37% of GLA, has operated at the center since opening in 1996; 80% of existing tenants have remained for over 10 years.
